rationale: C05 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. It concerns the same precise machinery: a private bill reopening the limitations period for an income-tax refund, followed by an explanation of the missed deadline and an almost verbatim policy paragraph about finality, discrimination against similarly situated taxpayers, and undesirable precedent. The child reproduces both C05's operative framing and its argumentative sequence, adapting the taxpayer, tax years, and asserted basis for refund. C11 and C19 contain closely related language, but C05 has the strongest overall match to the child's bill description and rationale.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The bill would provide that, notwithstanding any period of limitations or lapse of time, claims, exclusive of interest, for credit or refund of overpayments of income taxes for the taxable years 1951 and 1952 ... may be filed within one year after the date of enactment
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The bill would provide that, notwithstanding any statutory period of limitation, refund or credit shall be made or allowed to the beneficiary of any overpayment of income tax for the year 1951, if claim therefor is filed within one year after the date of enactment.
shared_material.explanation: The same operative mechanism and sentence structure reopen a limitations period for specified income-tax refunds for one year after enactment.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The statutory period of limitations, which Congress has included in the revenue system as a matter of sound policy, is essential in order to achieve finality in tax administration.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The statutory period of limitations, which the Congress has included in the revenue system as a matter of sound policy, is essential in order to achieve finality in tax administration.
shared_material.explanation: This is essentially verbatim and is the central policy justification in both directives.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Granting special relief in this case, where a refund was not claimed in the time and manner prescribed by law, would constitute a discrimination against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Granting special relief in this case would constitute a discrimination against other taxpayers similarly situated and would create an undesirable precedent.
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves C05's distinctive three-part conclusion, adding only a clause emphasizing the untimely claim.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Under the circumstances, therefore, I am constrained to withhold my approval of the bill.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: For these reasons I am constrained to withhold my approval from the bill.
shared_material.explanation: Both close the same sequence—limitations policy, discriminatory special relief, undesirable precedent, and withheld approval—with routine wording adapted slightly in the child.
